objective: Fostering psychological safety: promoting a no-blame culture, encouraging dialogue over debate, and normalizing challenges to the status quo

sources.cite: PMI, PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP) Examination Content Outline (March 2026): Mindset 28%, Leadership 25%, Product 19%, Delivery 28%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of PMI's PDF. Relevant text: Domain IV Task 1 'Seek early feedback' ('Deliver work in small increments'; 'Collect and incorporate stakeholders' feedback on a regular basis'); Task 3 'Manage impediments and risk' ('Proactively identify risks and impediments'; 'Prioritize impediment removal and risk mitigation activities'); Domain I Task 7 'Embrace Change' ('Embrace process adaptation by responding to changing requirements and priorities'; 'Adapt to product needs based on the learning and feedback'). The objective wording here is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's sprint-release-before-review-pmiacp (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The company, the product, the team and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the agile coach for a fictional team building a booking platform for Wexford Ferries. After an outage last month, the manager named the developer responsible in a company email. Since then the team has gone quiet.
handover: Retrospectives end in ten minutes with 'nothing to add'.
A junior developer privately says the current plan cannot meet the date.
howItWorks: The board shows the Sprint's commitments, the work, the impediments, the people's support and the Scrum events.
Move on a day at a time. A decision comes to you at each Daily Scrum; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Day 3: a developer notices a failing backup job and says nothing; the next incident loses a day of bookings.
Day 7: the retrospective lasts eight minutes; the junior developer keeps the date problem to herself.
Day 9: the team misses the date by four weeks; three people say they had seen it coming.

blamePrompt.title: A review that named a person

choices.label: With the manager's agreement, rerun the review blamelessly: how the system let one command take the site down, with fixes to the deploy safeguards, and the manager acknowledges the email was a mistake

effects.log: The review finds missing safeguards; the manager apologizes to the team.

choices.feedback: A no-blame culture looks for how the system allowed a failure, so people report problems instead of hiding them.

choices.label: Talk privately with the named developer
choices.feedback: Kind, but the team still sees blame as the norm.

choices.label: Move on; the incident is closed
choices.feedback: The team learns that mistakes are punished.

choices.label: Run the retrospective with working agreements, anonymous input first, and a facilitated dialogue in small groups where every view is explored before deciding

effects.log: The team raises seven issues, including the date.

choices.feedback: Psychological safety grows when people can raise views without risk and the team explores them through dialogue, not debate.

choices.label: Use an anonymous survey and skip the discussion
choices.feedback: Issues surface, but the team never talks them through.

choices.label: Have the manager run the retrospective to keep it on track
choices.feedback: With the person who sent the email in charge, nobody speaks.

challengePrompt.title: A junior developer challenges the plan
challengePrompt.context: She shows the plan cannot meet the date.

choices.label: Thank her in front of the team, examine her analysis with the product owner, and replan scope for the date openly

effects.log: The plan is reset; the date holds with smaller scope.

choices.feedback: Normalizing challenges to the status quo means acting on them visibly, so others raise the next one.

choices.label: Thank her privately and raise it yourself
choices.feedback: The issue is handled, but the team does not see challenges rewarded.

choices.label: Tell her the plan was approved and to focus on her tasks
choices.feedback: The team learns that questioning the plan is unwelcome.

parts.label: Blame and dialogue

parts.modelAnswer: We reran the outage review without blame and found missing deploy safeguards; the retrospective used working agreements, anonymous input and facilitated dialogue.

parts.label: Challenge
parts.criteria: The date challenge welcomed; scope replanned.

blameHarm.headline: No-blame reviews
blameHarm.body: Look at the system, not a person.

scoring.modelReasoning: Psychological safety lets people raise problems without fear. Build it with blameless reviews that examine the system, retrospectives with working agreements and facilitated dialogue, and visible appreciation and action when someone challenges the status quo.
